correctness.rationale: For Q4 with distinct sensor sites and one erasure, all 560 triples are partitioned into six translation/coordinate-permutation orbits; direct forcing proves a triple succeeds exactly when it contains a Hamming-distance-three pair. No one-failure triple is possible because the auxiliary distance-three graph is bipartite. A robust four-set corresponds precisely to an induced 2K2/P4/C4 in the auxiliary graph, isomorphic to Q4. Elementary counts give 160+192+24=376. Two separately implemented exhaustive programs independently reconstruct these four-sets, five symmetry orbits, 2496 token-jump edges, radius 5/diameter 6, and zero original-cube token slides; one directly checks power domination of all 65536 subsets, while the second uses the structural criterion and complete BFS. No extrapolation beyond Q4.

value.rationale: Motivated by exact one-sensor failure resilience, the result gives a complete natural configuration census for a symmetric graph, with a structural correspondence to three types of induced four-vertex subgraphs in a second cube, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. Its five orbit types and the sharp immobility-vs-connectivity separation under physical slides versus unrestricted replacement quantify the topology and flexibility of minimal robust sensor placements. Both are meaningful graph-structure phenomena beyond the already-known ordinary minimum and are fully finite and reproducible.
